perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, the available information is:

- I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. Arthur Begum is my police-officer friend; we have a professional relationship that became a friendship, and I often seek his advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated and our progress was suffering. I arranged to meet Arthur at a coffee shop. I told him I needed advice, that my team seemed completely unmotivated and it was affecting progress, and that I was at my wit’s end. Arthur said motivation can be tricky, asked if I had tried understanding what drives each team member individually, and advised one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood. I admitted I had focused on goals/deadlines, said I would try his suggestion, thanked him, and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward I felt hopeful and relieved. I believed Arthur’s advice would help, so I implemented it with my team: I told them we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand their motivations. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- Later I noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried, so I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding and I was worried about the project’s future. Arthur said that was tough, suggested there might be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and said I might need to dig deeper. I agreed to set up another round of meetings and thanked him.
- I became determined and focused. I believed there might be underlying team issues I had not addressed, so I held one-on-one meetings. I asked for concerns/problems. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few team members and it was affecting work. I said I would look into resolving conflicts and asked if there was anything else. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. I said I would see about redistributing tasks and that their well-being was important.
- I felt optimistic and empowered. I believed addressing individual concerns would improve performance, so I told the team we would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive and open environment. Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good their concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and that their input and well-being are crucial.

I do not have access to hidden causes, private thoughts, or events not stated or observed above.
